To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel electrodeposition process was developed to deposit nanotwinned Cu within a deep TSV with a high aspect-ratio, which was achieved by adding the gelatin additive into the copper deposition solution.
a large-scale nanotwinned columnar copper was fabricated by direct current electrodeposition within a 3D through silicon via with a high aspect-ratio.
we have developed a new method for the direct-current electroplating of nanotwinned Cu in 3D TSVs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication and characterization of nanotwinned Cu within TSV, which is a key step for the development of 3D integrated circuits.
the development of a novel electrodeposition method, which can be potentially used for the fabrication of high-aspect-ratio nanotwinned metals.
the large-scale electrodeposition of columnarr nanotwinned Cu within 3D TSV, which is a key step for the application of nanotwinned metals in microelectronic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a large-scale nanotwinned columnar copper with a high aspectratio was successfully electrodeposited within the TSV by a bottom-up approach.

the large-scale nanotwinned array was fabricated in a TSV by the bottom–up electrodeposition method with a gelatin additive, which would be beneficial to the further development of the 3D integrated circuit.

a large-scale nanotwinned Cu array with a high aspectratio (~4), a low current density (10 mA/cm2), and a high deposition rate (2.4 mm/min) could be achieved by a bottom–up electrodeposition technique with a gelatin additive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electrodeposition of nanotwinned metals in 3D TSVs could be a promising way for fabricating high-quality nanotwinned metal array with uniform microstructure and mechanical properties, which is very difficult to achieve by other means.

this paper presents an innovative approach for the fabrication of a high-quality nanotwinned array with a large-scale and high-aspect-ratio, which is a significant step toward the application of nanotwinned metal in microelectronics and microelectronic packaging.
the nanotwinned structure can be obtained within the whole TSV by a bottom–up electrodeposition method, which is promising to improve the reliability of TSV interconnects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a large-scale nanotwinned Cu array can be directly fabricated by the electrodeposition method, which is promising for the fabrication of 3D micro/nanoelectronic devices.
the nanotwinned microstructure could be obtained by a bottom–up electrochemical process, which is a promising approach to fabricate large-scale TSVs with high aspect ratios.
the gelatin additive can be applied in the electroplating process of other metals and alloys to obtain the desired microstructure.
